The unified ray marching loop handles both forward (rendering) and backward (back-projection) passes.
- **Synchronization Stalls:** Data scattering during back-projection (texture writes) causes stalls because neighboring rays write to the same voxels.
- **Time Complexity:** Depends on the number of CG iterations and the cost of ray marching per iteration.
- **Memory Complexity:** $O(N_v)$ for volume storage, where $N_v$ is the number of voxels.
- **When Not to Use:** When high precision is critical and 16-bit textures are insufficient.
It builds on the linearity of light transport and the sparsity of the rendering operator.
